_: Human tooth enamel: ~96 % mineral (carbonated hydroxyapatite in rods 4-8 um wide), translucent, the outer layer of the crown up to ~2.5 mm thick at the cusps and thin at the cervix. Values for permanent adult teeth at room or body temperature, hydrated (in vivo enamel is always wet with saliva and a protein pellicle). Stiffness and hardness fall from the outer surface toward the dentin-enamel junction (DEJ). Materials research lane, mouth group, 2026-11-07.

alpha.src: polished-looking natural enamel with perikymata (fine growth lines) - a glossy dielectric, not a mirror; not measured

thickness_um.src: not found on teeth (MTT section 10); palate 11-30 um (ASSY23) is the nearest

mu_s_per_cm.src: FRIED95 enamel 15-105 cm-1 from 1.06 um down to 543 nm (more scattering at shorter wavelength)

g.src: FRIED95 HG g 0.96 plus a 30-60 % isotropic component

isotropic_fraction.src: FRIED95 (36 % at 1053 nm, Darling 2006 via search)

translucency_parameter_1mm.src: YU09 TP 18.7 for 1 mm human enamel (via MTT D16); TP falls with thickness, rises with wavelength

colour_Lab_2mm.src: ARDU10 in vivo enamel 2 mm (via MTT section 4)

translucency.v: high: enamel transmits and forward-scatters; the colour of a tooth is mostly the dentin seen through it; incisal edges with no dentin behind look bluish-grey (opalescence: short wavelengths scattered more)
translucency.src: FRIED95 mu_s rising toward blue; MTT section 4

kinetic.src: DOUGLAS85 enamel on enamel in an artificial mouth 0.10-0.42; fluid type had little effect, surface roughness a large one

surface_energy_mJ_m2.src: SFE_CPC from contact angles: ground/polished 88 +- 8, saliva-coated 103 +- 4 (a 1983 study found the pellicle lowers it; methods differ)

restitution.src: not found for teeth; a stiff brittle mineral solid against a rigid flat at ~1 m/s rebounds strongly (ceramics 0.8-0.95); impact on a tooth is mostly governed by the soft periodontal ligament behind it

water_contact_angle_deg.src: porcine enamel 50 +- 18 deg (search result); human polished enamel 'consistent with literature' not retrieved; saliva pellicle makes it more hydrophilic

hardness.src: HV_MR enamel HV 315-357 (stored teeth); CUY02 nanoindentation 5.35 GPa occlusal surface -> 2.83 near DEJ (buccal up to 6.17); ZHANG14 surface max ~3.5 GPa; Mohs 5 = apatite by definition (MOHS; enamel D from its mineral)

abrasion.src: LAMB89 steady-state occlusal contact wear over 4 years

porosity.src: enamel is ~96 % mineral with ~1 % water by weight in its pores (recalled textbook); not measured here

collision_thickness_mm.src: numerical skin for a rigid solid; the salivary pellicle is ~0.1-1 um (not measured here), so 1 um holds it

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: rigid relative to every soft tissue: use Hertz with E 90 GPa, nu 0.3 rather than a linear ramp

contact_damping_ratio.src: ceramic-like solid, almost no internal damping

response_time_ms.src: hard-on-hard Hertz impacts last tens to hundreds of microseconds (depends on mass and radius)

damping_ratio.src: ceramic-like solid, almost no internal damping

deform.model_note: linear elastic until fracture; graded (stiffer at the surface); the rods make it mildly anisotropic and the DEJ arrests cracks

E_GPa.src: CUY02 nanoindentation mapping 98.1 -> 71.4 GPa (buccal up to 142); TOOTHREV 70-110 GPa

poisson.src: commonly used value for enamel in FE studies (recalled, unverified)

toughness_MPa_m05.src: PARK08 apparent indentation K_c young / old enamel; TOOTHREV 0.7-2.1 (direction-dependent, higher across the rods)

viscoelastic.v: very small creep from the ~4 % organic and water fraction (ZHANG14 reviews it); treat as elastic

xpbd_compliance_per_Pa.src: 1/E with E = 90 GPa; effectively rigid in a body sim

effusivity.src: sqrt(k rho c) with k 0.93, rho 2970, c 750

wet.src: in vivo enamel is always coated

dehydrated.src: air-dried enamel looks whiter and more opaque (water in the pores replaced by air raises scattering), reversible within minutes to hours of rewetting (clinical shade-matching guidance; numbers not retrieved)

aged.src: MTT R14: teeth darken and gain chroma with age to ~46 y; older enamel K_c slightly lower (PARK08)
